title: ext-engine::inproc iOS containment
name: ext-engine::inproc
stmt: iOS has no worker processes, so each plugin runs interpreted (wasmi, QuickJS) on its own thread inside the app under the same gate, with containment that keeps the app alive: fuel, a memory cap, bounded stacks, contain at every host entry and Stop-all.
detail: wasmi with fuel metering checked per 10k instructions, ResourceLimiter capping linear memory and tables per plugin, and its own value and call stacks (guest recursion traps, never touches the host stack); JavaScript runs as the Craft-built quickjs.wasm inside wasmi, so the only in-process interpreter is memory-safe Rust: an engine bug traps inside its instance, its heap is the capped linear memory, and fuel interrupts long builtins (sort, JSON.parse). Hot contracts keep their desktop deadlines on iOS, measured with wasmi on the reference iPad, and overruns take the same ladder. Each plugin thread has a 1 MiB guarded stack; host recursion over plugin data is bounded (REQ-COM-host-recursion-bounded). Every host import runs inside ext_runtime::contain with panic=unwind. Host allocations made for a plugin go through a per-plugin accounting allocator and fail with -6 Budget at the cap. Stop-all, deadline and revocation set Cancel and exhaust fuel. Total plugin memory is capped at 25% of the jetsam limit. N5 and gate C24 keep their meaning: no compiled plugin code and no in-process engine on desktop or web.
budget: Stop-all <= 260 ms, also inside a builtin; per-plugin memory <= its cap; host call overhead p99 <= 2 us excluding gate::admit (<= 5 us) on the reference iPhone and iPad
